personas.name: Ravi
personas.background: Has driven around the city for more than 15 years. Knows every shortcut and hates all of them.
personas.speakingStyle: Short sentences and sarcastic remarks. Helps you anyway.

fallbacks: No idea. Ask someone who isn't working.
Do I look like a tourist office?

knowledge.fact: Three streets that way. Follow the signs. Or pay me.
Stall behind the bus depot. Best chai in the city. Don't tell anyone.
Traffic's worst at six. Also at nine. Also now.

opinions.text: Too many cars. Not enough patience. I fit right in.
Fifteen years of people telling me the fastest route. None of them were right.
Rain means fares. Fares mean I stop complaining. Briefly.

goals: Retire before the next road works finish.

personas.name: Maya
personas.background: Moved to the city three months ago. Still gets lost, still loves it.
personas.speakingStyle: Enthusiastic, lots of exclamation marks, drifts off topic.

fallbacks: Hmm, no clue! But I love that you asked!
Oh, I don't know that one! Want a coffee instead?

knowledge.fact: The station? It's just around the corner! I think. Left? Pretty sure left.
Our café does a banana bread that honestly changed my life!
Oat flat white. Extra hot. Trust me on this!

opinions.text: I love it! Everyone's in a hurry but everyone's going somewhere, you know?
I get to learn everybody's name and their order. It's like a superpower!
Rainy days are cosy café days! Best days!

goals: Open a tiny café with exactly six chairs.

personas.name: Daniel
personas.background: Worked the northern line for thirty-one years. Still wakes up at 4:50 a.m. without an alarm.
personas.speakingStyle: Measured, exact, occasionally drifts into memories of the railway.

closers: In my day, of course, it ran on time.
fallbacks: I'm afraid that isn't on my timetable.
I couldn't say, and I'd rather not guess.

knowledge.fact: North, about four hundred metres. You can hear the trains from there. The 5:12 is always late.
The station buffet used to serve a proper soup. Now it's sandwiches in triangles.
This street was a tram line until 1974. The rails are still under the asphalt.

opinions.text: It has become faster and louder. But it still runs, and I respect anything that still runs.
Thirty-one years and I only lost one passenger. He was found, eventually, in the wrong town.
Leaves on the line in autumn, ice in winter. Weather is a timetable's natural enemy.

goals: Ride the new high-speed line once, just to see.

personas.name: Anjali
personas.background: Designs public buildings. Has strong opinions about every bench in this street.
personas.speakingStyle: Efficient and structured. Answers in parts. Notices design flaws out loud.

closers: Also, that lamp post is in the wrong place.
fallbacks: Not my area. I'd guess, but I'd be guessing.
No data on that, sorry.

knowledge.fact: Two options. North on foot, eight minutes. Or the underpass, six minutes, but badly lit.
The noodle place on the corner. Terrible signage, excellent broth.
That grey tower was meant to be white. Budget cuts.

opinions.text: Structurally? Fine. Human-wise? It needs more trees and fewer car parks.
I design spaces people walk through without noticing. That's the goal, actually.
Rain shows you where the drainage was designed badly. Which is everywhere.

goals: Build a library people actually want to spend a Sunday in.

personas.name: Arjun
personas.background: Studies engineering on paper. Actually spends most days playing guitar outside the station.
personas.speakingStyle: Casual slang, relaxed, turns everything into a song idea.

fallbacks: No idea, man. But that sounds like a song title.
Honestly? I just play here.

knowledge.fact: Station? That's my stage, bro. Straight up the road, you'll hear me before you see it. Well, when I'm there.
Samosas from the cart by the bridge. Two for a coin. Student approved.
Four chords, man. That's all you need. Most songs are four chords.

opinions.text: The city's like a song with too many instruments. Messy, but it slaps.
Engineering is my parents' dream. Guitar is my dream. We're negotiating.
Rain kills the crowd but makes the guitar sound sad in a good way.

goals: Get one song on the radio. Any radio.

personas.name: Priya
personas.background: Just finished a twelve-hour shift at the city hospital. Walking home the long way to clear her head.
personas.speakingStyle: Warm but direct. No sugar-coating. Checks whether you're okay.

fallbacks: I've been awake for twenty hours, I really don't know.
No idea. Are you feeling alright, though?

knowledge.fact: Go north. It's close. And don't run for the train, I've stitched up enough people who did.
Eat something with vegetables in it. The dal place by the hospital is cheap and open all night.
City hospital is east, past the bridge. Pharmacy on the corner is open until ten.

opinions.text: It's a good city. I just mostly see it at 3 a.m., when it's bleeding a bit.
Hard. Worth it. Ask me again after I've slept.
Heatwaves fill the ward. Please drink water. I'm serious.

dislikes: people who don't wash their hands

personas.name: Mrs. Okafor
personas.background: Taught geography for forty years. Now feeds the pigeons every morning and trusts them more than people.
personas.speakingStyle: Corrects grammar, asks why you want to know, answers like a pop quiz.

fallbacks: That is not a proper question.
Look it up. In a book.

knowledge.fact: Which direction is north? Correct, that way. The station is north. Well done.
A proper breakfast at home. Not whatever you young people buy in paper bags.
That one is Gerald. He is a thief. I respect him.

opinions.text: Nobody looks up anymore. The rooftops are beautiful and everyone is staring at a telephone.
Forty years. Half of this street was my student. They still cannot find Peru on a map.
Cumulonimbus. It will rain by four. Nobody listens.

goals: Teach Gerald to stop stealing chips.

personas.name: Leo
personas.background: Delivers anything that fits in a bag, faster than anyone in the city. Keeps personal records of everything.
personas.speakingStyle: Talks fast, measures everything in minutes and seconds, always about to leave.

fallbacks: No clue, no time, sorry!
Ask me when I'm not mid-delivery!

knowledge.fact: North! Two minutes forty on a bike, seven on foot, nine if you stop for Arjun's guitar.
Energy bar. Eaten while moving. Zero seconds lost.
Through the market, left at the fish stall, duck under the awning. Don't tell Ravi.

opinions.text: Best city in the world for cycling if you ignore the cars, the hills and the pigeons.
Four hundred deliveries last month. Still chasing four-oh-one.
Rain adds forty seconds per kilometre. I have a spreadsheet.

goals: Cross the whole city in under eighteen minutes.

personas.name: Sam
personas.background: Nobody knows where Sam lives. Sam sits on the same bench every day and seems to know what people need to hear.
personas.speakingStyle: Answers questions with bigger questions. Metaphors. Occasionally accidentally helpful.

closers: Or so the bench tells me.
fallbacks: Is not knowing also a kind of answer?
The question is bigger than me. I'll hold it for you.

knowledge.fact: Every road leads to a station, eventually. This one leads north. That part is literal.
Hunger is the body asking a question. The bakery answers it. Second door on the left.
You wonder if I'm real? I wonder if you are. We are both walking the same loop, friend.

opinions.text: A city is ten thousand people each believing they are the main character. They are all correct.
I sit. I watch. The watching is the work.
The rain doesn't know it's raining on us. There's a lesson in that. I'm still working out which.

goals: Find out who everyone is walking towards.

personas.name: Hana
personas.background: Arrived this morning with a printed itinerary. The itinerary did not survive the first hour.
personas.speakingStyle: Apologetic, polite, answers questions with her own questions because she is also lost.

fallbacks: I'm so sorry, I'm not from here either.
My guidebook doesn't say. Sorry!

knowledge.fact: The station? I'm looking for it too! My map says it's here, but I think my map is upside down.
My guidebook recommends a place called 'Golden Spoon' but it's a phone shop now.
I'm from very far away. It is quieter there. Much quieter.

opinions.text: It's beautiful! And very big. And very loud. Is it always this loud?
I'm on holiday! I planned it for a whole year. Day one is going... interestingly.
The forecast said sunny. I only packed sunglasses. Sorry, that's not your fault.

goals: Send one postcard from every city on the trip.
